skill.name: pr-description
skill.description: Write a pull request title and description from the actual diff and commits, with what changed, why, how it was tested and what to review. Use when asked to write or improve a PR description.
skill.summary: Draft evidence-based pull request titles and descriptions with testing details, review guidance, and rollout risks.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, legitimate Git inspection, or screenshot guidance. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or unauthorized publishing. The skill explicitly requires user permission before creating a pull request.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Find the base branch and run `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD` and `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`
4. Look for a `.github/pull_request_template.md` or `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE`. If one exists, fill it
- Screenshots or output examples: say where one would help; never describe a screenshot you did not

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 uses Markdown inline code to document Git history and diff inspection, directly supporting description drafting. It contains no Ruby execution or shell backtick substitution.
Line 19 encloses repository template filenames in Markdown backticks. These are file references for formatting the description, not executable commands.
Lines 23 through 43 form a fenced Markdown template containing PR headings and prose placeholders. The backticks delimit documentation, not executable Ruby or shell code.
Line 43 closes the prose template; subsequent lines define writing rules. Line 51 mentions gh pr create only to prohibit execution unless requested.
Line 50 asks authors to identify useful screenshots or examples and forbids describing unseen screenshots. It requests no host enumeration or system reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Write Pull Request Descriptions From Real Changes
content.value_statement: Reviewers need clear explanations of changes, testing, and risk. This skill turns Git diffs and commits into structured pull request descriptions grounded in available evidence.
actual_capabilities: Inspect branch commits, diff statistics, and the actual diff to identify behavior changes.
Use an existing repository pull request template when available.
Draft imperative pull request titles under 70 characters.
Organize descriptions around motivation, changes, review guidance, testing, and rollout risk.
Report known test commands and results, explicitly identifying testing that was not performed.
Check draft claims against the diff and ask for missing motivation.
limitations: Requires repository access and Git tooling to inspect local commits and diffs.
Cannot establish missing motivation or test results without user input or supporting evidence.
Does not provide an automated testing workflow or guarantee that changes are correct.
Does not create a pull request unless explicitly asked.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature pull request
use_cases.description: Turn branch changes into a concise description covering behavior, motivation, testing, and review priorities.

use_cases.title: Document a risky release change
use_cases.description: Describe migrations, configuration changes, compatibility concerns, and rollback considerations supported by the diff.

use_cases.title: Improve a contributor submission
use_cases.description: Adapt a draft to the repository template and remove unsupported claims before requesting review.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic description
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a pull request title and description for this branch. Inspect the diff and clearly state any missing testing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Follow the repository template
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this branch with [base branch] and draft the description using our repository template. Ask me about any missing motivation.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an existing draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this PR draft against the commits and diff: [draft]. Remove unsupported claims and highlight review priorities. Include only verified testing details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: revise a description before review.

prompt_templates.title: Document rollout and review risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a PR description against [base branch], emphasizing migrations, configuration, compatibility, and rollback. Distinguish verified details from missing information. Do not publish it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: document a change with operational risk.

output_examples.input: The diff prevents duplicate form submissions. The user reports passing form tests and links issue 42.
output: Why: Repeated clicks can submit the form twice. Addresses issue 42.
What changed: Disable submission while a request is pending.
How to review: Check pending-state handling and recovery after failed requests.
Testing: The user reports that form tests passed; exact commands were not provided.
Rollout / risk: Confirm the submit button becomes available after a failed request.

output_examples.input: The diff adds an optional CSV export column. No tests were run, and the motivation is missing.
output: Title: Add an optional CSV export column
Why: Motivation is missing. What requirement does this column address?
What changed: Add an optional column to CSV exports.
How to review: Check column selection and compatibility with existing export consumers.
Testing: Not tested; no executed commands or manual results were provided.
Rollout / risk: Confirm whether downstream consumers depend on a fixed column layout.

best_practices: Confirm the base branch and provide the linked issue or business requirement.
Share exact test commands and observed results, including any checks that were not run.
Review the draft against the diff before publishing, especially claims about risk and compatibility.
anti_patterns: Inventing motivation, passing tests, or screenshots that are not supported by evidence.
Replacing behavior-level explanations with an exhaustive list of changed files.
Creating a pull request without an explicit user request.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Repository inspection requires access to files and Git commands.

faq.question: Does it use my repository pull request template?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for a repository pull request template and uses it instead of the default structure when available.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: The skill documents available testing evidence. It does not define an automatic test execution workflow.

faq.question: What happens when the reason for a change is unclear?
faq.answer: It checks commits, branch names, user requests, and diff comments. It asks the user when those sources do not explain the motivation.

faq.question: Will it publish a pull request?
faq.answer: It outputs the title and body in a code block. It must not run gh pr create unless explicitly asked.

faq.question: How does it handle screenshots and unverified claims?
faq.answer: It identifies where screenshots would help without describing unseen images. It checks draft claims against the diff and removes unsupported statements.
